title: How Does a Cockroach Sense You? Explained Simply | PUC Biology
description:
A light flicks on in a dark kitchen and a cockroach is gone in a second. Aarav asks: how did it sense him so fast? And how does a body with no bones keep its shape?

You will meet Periplaneta americana and its chitin exoskeleton of sclerites and arthrodial membranes, then zoom from the thorax to the head and the mouth parts (labrum, mandibles, maxillae, labium, hypopharynx). We build the wings and abdomen step by step (tegmina, hind wings, genital pouch, anal cerci and styles), follow food through the crop and gizzard, see breathing through tracheae and spiracles, the open blood system, Malpighian tubules and the chain of ganglia, with a pause and think. Then a worked example from ootheca to nymph to adult, the exam trap about blood flow, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: The cockroach is not in the current rationalised NCERT text but is in the ISC (CISCE) Class 11 syllabus.

This is Episode 59 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
